title: Defaults generated by a Supplier per constant

blocks.text: The page's fifth workaround, the Supplier-based pattern, gives each enum constant a `Supplier<?>` instead of a value. The value is made when it is asked for, so a constant can hand out a **new** mutable default each time, which a single stored value cannot. The page's rule of thumb: use it when values vary per call, not when one stable, cached value is wanted.
Complete the enum `LazyDefault` (the constants and their suppliers are given):

items: `<T> T generate()` returns a value made by the constant's supplier, made anew on every call.
`<T> T generateAs(Class<T> type)` does the same, but checks the value with `type` and throws `ClassCastException` inside the method when it does not fit.

cases.says: generate() returns the value the constant's Supplier makes: an empty list, an empty map, or a new StringBuilder.
Each generate() or generateAs() call makes a new value, for every constant, so filling one list or map does not show up in the next.
generateAs() with the wrong Class throws ClassCastException itself, even when the caller ignores the result.

concepts: Storing a Supplier per constant makes a new value on every call, for defaults that must not be shared.
